job.direction: One station only, complete and isolated, with genuinely transparent background. Match the Transport world camera and calm roof/wall masses. The full image is one 16 m square parcel, with transparent margins; preserve the complete parcel-to-cell scale. Position the bottom contact of the station platform at 95.3 percent of cell height. Keep a broad 2:1 dimetric ground platform, almost filling the parcel width but inset from its edges. Do not include rails, trains, vehicles, grass, decorative text or unrelated surroundings. entries.name: Small railway station
entries.description: A clearly recognizable small railway station, visually different from an open bus shelter: a compact enclosed single-storey cream-plaster ticket hall about 6 m wide and 4 m deep at the rear side of a long low stone platform; one slate-green broad pitched roof, a personnel door and two large blue-grey window panes; a connected long platform canopy supported by only two stout dark timber posts beside the hall; a simple broad bench, and one compact signal mast with a single red signal arm. Hall walls 3 m high, ordinary door 2.1 m high and 0.95 m wide. Station house, roof and canopy are the large identifying features. Platform length about 13 m and width 4 m; building and canopy together fit within the one-tile 16 m square parcel. Roof ridge follows the platform axis. Few large shapes, broad flat stone and roof tones, extremely restrained painted texture. No brick joints or roof tiles, no tiny lettering, no railings, no people, no clock tower, no grand station, no decorative noise.

prompt:
Fixed orthographic 2:1 dimetric camera: ground edges at +26.565 and -26.565 degrees, vertical walls, two visible facades, no perspective convergence.
Quiet hand-painted miniature architecture with clean silhouettes, broad roof and wall colour masses, restrained warm materials, northwest daylight and soft contact shadows.
A consistent world scale: one tile is 16 metres square. A person is 1.75m tall; ordinary personnel doors are 2.1m high and 0.95m wide; storeys are 3m; windows are about 1.2m high; low fences are 1.2m. Vehicle loading bays are 4.2m high and visibly distinct from personnel doors.
Bigger buildings gain additional rooms, wings, floors and repeated bays at the SAME human scale. Never enlarge doors, windows, people, garden fences or benches to fill a bigger parcel.
Designed to remain recognizable at Region 0.5x and Town 1x: distinctive roofline, clear facade shading, a few large openings and broad planted clusters. No individual bricks, roof tiles, woodgrain scratches, tiny lettering, tiny flower dots, dense crate grids, fine handrails, thin window mullions or decorative speckle.
Preserve useful large identifiers such as loading sheds, silos, greenhouses, chimneys, awnings and sports surfaces. No people as decorative scale filler, no text or logos.
Genuine transparent background, isolated complete sprites with generous transparent gutters. No scenery outside the parcel, no backdrop cards or opaque plinth. Gardens blend with the climate terrain.
Production 1x1 atlas, exactly 1 slots in row-major order; each cell represents the stated full parcel, not a close-up of the building. Follow each slot's parcel-to-cell calibration: equal footprints share one pixel-to-metre scale; larger footprints have proportionally smaller doors in the normalized cell so they render at the same world height. Do not give different footprint tiers equal door pixel heights. Do not independently fit each building's bounding box.
Temperate green grass, muted red brick, pale plaster, timber, slate and terracotta roofs.
